CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left wrist pain with numbness and tingling in fingers.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper who presents with left wrist pain and numbness/tingling in the fingers for several months. Onset was gradual without identifiable precipitant. Symptoms are worse at night, with patient waking from sleep with paresthesias and numbness in the hand that improves with manual manipulation. Numbness affects all fingers but is more pronounced in the thumb and index finger; the fifth finger is occasionally affected. Associated left hand weakness and grip difficulty, with patient reporting difficulty maintaining hold on objects and dropping items. Right hand without significant current symptoms. Occupational history significant for repetitive heavy labor as a landscaper, including frequent raking and digging with the same movements performed daily. Denies history of rheumatoid arthritis or other joint/neurologic conditions.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Focused on chief complaint. Denies systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history documented. Denies rheumatoid arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
No current medications reported.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a landscaper performing yard work and maintenance, including flower bed upkeep. Work is described as heavy labor with repetitive daily motions. Alcohol consumption consists of 1-2 beers on Friday and Saturday evenings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Neurological: Grip strength weaker on left hand compared to right hand. Sensation to light touch intact bilaterally; however, patient reports altered sensation on the thumb side compared to the index finger side. Wrist exam: Percussion over the dorsal wrist bilaterally elicits tingling and electric sensation ("zinging") in the fingertips, indicating positive Tinel's sign bilaterally.

RESULTS
EMG (electromyography) study ordered to confirm diagnosis and assess severity.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, early stage, with predominant symptoms on the left side. Likely etiology is repetitive occupational stress from landscaping work.

Plan:
1. Activity modification: Reduce repetitive wrist motions by delegating heavier tasks to other employees for 2 weeks.
2. Wrist splint: Prescribed for symptomatic relief and to reduce pressure on median nerve.
3. Medications: Ibuprofen 600 mg PO every 6 hours for pain and inflammation.
4. Diagnostics: EMG study to confirm diagnosis and assess nerve involvement.
5. Follow-up: Return to office in 2 weeks to assess response to conservative treatment. Will determine need for additional intervention including possible surgical decompression if conservative measures prove inadequate.
